title: Either sense of justify still fits Paul: free absolution and free sanctification
source_text: XXXV. Secundo observandum est, aliis illis locis magis contentiosis, & de quibus nulla lis est Protestantibus inter se, sed cum Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae, quocunque sensu sumatur justificandi verbum, sive, scilicet, restringatur ad solam absolutionem a reatu peccati; sive nostram quoque sanctificationem complecti censeatur, sensum semper fore commodum, & Apostolico stylo, ac analogiae fidei congruentem. Sicut enim verum est nos a peccatis absolvi, gratis per Christi gratiam, sic etiam gratis, & per Christi gratiam sanctificamur, & regeneramur. Item sicut Deus impium a peccatis absolvit, ita quoque eundem Spiritu suo sanctificat. Sicuti per fidem remittuntur peccata, sic etiam fide corda purificantur & sanctificantur. Denique quemadmodum absolutio nostra non est ex operibus, ita quoque nostra sanctificatio, seu regeneratio, juxta stylum & phrasin Apostoli, ex operibus esse dicenda non est.
pass_a_gloss: Second it is to be observed that in those other more contentious places, concerning which there is no quarrel among Protestants among themselves but with the Doctors of the Roman Church, in whichever sense the verb of justifying is taken—whether, namely, it is restricted to mere absolution from the guilt of sin, or is judged to embrace our sanctification also—the sense will always be fitting and congruent with the Apostolic style and the analogy of faith. For just as it is true that we are absolved from sins freely through Christ's grace, so also freely and through Christ's grace we are sanctified and regenerated. Likewise just as God absolves the ungodly from sins, so also he sanctifies the same by his Spirit. As through faith sins are remitted, so also by faith hearts are purified and sanctified. Finally just as our absolution is not of works, so also our sanctification or regeneration, according to the Apostle's style and phrasing, is not to be said to be of works.
pass_b_english: On contested Paul texts, either lexical take still yields an Apostolic, analogy-of-faith sense.
Absolution and sanctification alike are free by Christ's grace and faith—not of works.
